The story

Track open, km

Conventional railways 1830–1911: Jeremy Atack, "Historical Geographic Information Systems (GIS) database of U.S. Railroads for 1830–1911" (Vanderbilt University), track in operation by each survey year. Between two survey years, new track is spread out in order of distance from the existing network, so exact opening years are approximate. The database ends in 1911; the network kept growing to a peak of about 410,000 km around 1916 and has since shrunk to about 220,000 km, which this map does not show. High-speed rail: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) routes of the Acela (Washington–Boston, 2000) and Brightline (Miami–West Palm Beach 2018, Orlando 2023). Acela reaches high speed only on parts of the corridor. · Highcharts.com
